title: Herbert Leary, Offshore Lounge, trip west and freelancing
summary: Late 1950s jobs with Herbert Leary and Jimmy Davis, a trip to San Francisco to bury his sister, a Florida trip, then freelancing with Emma Barrett and others.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: And you were the house band, Dale?

Well, the house band, well, that was Bill Matthews house band. Bill Matthews was there. Yeah, yeah, mm-hmm. And that was wrong, I think, wrong about, uh, uh, it must have been about 58, or something like that, when, when, when they let us go, see. Well, at that time, I started jobbing around with different fellas and everything, in, uh, I see, 58, 59, yeah. In round about 59, I joined Herbert Leary band during the Mardi Gras season. Mm-hmm. Well, I played that season with him. In round about, uh, 60, I went back with this fella, Jimmy Davis. Mm-hmm. We had a trio, uh, Andrew Johnson on drums, Jimmy Davis on piano, and, uh, me on electric guitar, and we was using Blanche Thomas at the time. Oh, the vocalist, yeah. Vocalist, yeah. Uh, well, we worked places like, uh, the Offshore Lounge, and, uh, and, uh, work at the Coat of Two Sisters. Mm-hmm. And, uh, work at another place out on Gentile called Guy's, Guy's Place, I remember. So, uh, and, uh, then my sister passed in July of 60, and I went out to San Francisco, stayed out there about two weeks, and I went to the place where old irons work, the hangover, the place where, uh, kid already works. I believe they call that, uh, river supplement or waterfront or something.
Did you play out there at all?

No, I just, I didn't take no instrument either, because I went out there to bury my sister, but I went around to those places. Mm-hmm. And I passed through Chicago, coming back, around about, uh, oh, yeah, that was around September, yeah. I stayed around there about ten days, and I went to the musician local, saw friends around there, the president, Harry Gray and Samuel Mitchell, uh, recording secretary, I believe. Mm-hmm. And, uh, when I came back here, the group I was working was still working at the Offshore Lounge, so we had about two more weeks there.
Mm-hmm. That was the Jim Davis?

Yeah, Jim Davis, Jimmy Davis, yeah. That closed, and then, uh, William picked me up in September, and I went to, to Florida. Mm-hmm. To September, October, I believe. We had about five weeks out there.
And when I came back, well, that's where I start, uh, working with, uh, not working, but I mean getting jobs with Emma Barrett and Paul Barberin and, uh, Noon and the Bazooka Man.

Yeah, and I also got a, guys up to date, uh, through Bill Mathes, you see. Mm-hmm. Yeah. So I think that, that carried me up to the day. I'm just what you say called freelancing, you know? Yeah, yeah, yeah. Playing with, uh, different fellas. Yeah.
